Music

  • Overview
  • Majors
  • Endorsements
  • Minors
  • Courses

Mission

It is the mission of the Department of Music at Chadron State College to provide students a rich environment in which to pursue their musical interests and career goals. With a broad-based curriculum, the undergraduate programs offered are designed to prepare students for a variety of careers in both the public and the private sectors. The CSC Department of Music strives to set and maintain high standards of excellence in providing musical leadership to the campus and to the service region as the premier four-year institution of higher education in the Nebraska Panhandle.

Student Learning Outcomes

Students will:

  • Perform music alone and in ensembles.
  • Analyze music using standard music vocabulary.
  • Synthesize the various aspects of musical information.

Admission to the Music Program

Incoming students are admitted to the music programs on a probationary basis. Admission is based on the following criteria:

  1. Students must successfully pass MUS 199 ADMISSION TO CANDIDACY in order to continue in any music program. Admission to Candidacy is comprised of an evaluation of the student’s progress in their major performance area as well as their piano, theory, and aural skills. A satisfactory evaluation will qualify a student to proceed to 200-level applied lessons.
  2. Students must also successfully perform a MUS 299 SOPHOMORE QUALIFYING EXAM for entrance to 300-level applied lessons. A student must demonstrate, through performance of technical material and repertoire, a degree of facility and musicality deemed sufficient to undertake advanced applied study.

Proficiencies and Requirements

  1. Music majors and minors are encouraged to participate in the major performing ensemble directly related to their major performing instrument/voice throughout their entire program, excluding the professional year for education majors and during internship (music industry option). These ensembles include Wind Symphony and Concert Choir for the Bachelor of Science degree programs, and Wind Symphony, Concert Choir, and Guitar Ensemble for the Bachelor of Arts. 
  2. Attendance at department-approved musical programs is required of all full-time music majors and minors enrolled in applied music lessons. Students enrolled in applied music major or minor lessons must also be co-enrolled in MUS 101 STUDENT RECITAL.
  3. New incoming students must take the theory and piano placement exams during the first week of classes.
  4. The Department of Music requires that music majors and minors receive a grade of “C” or higher in all music coursework in order to receive departmental approval for graduation.
  5. In accordance with standards set by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM), all majors will develop an awareness of non-Western music. To satisfy the requirement, all music majors will complete the following course:

MUS 116 PIANO CLASS FOUNDATIONS I1 Credit

Beginning-level piano instruction for music majors and minors with little or no prior keyboard experience.

MUS 117 PIANO CLASS FOUNDATIONS II1 Credit

Continuation of MUS 116. Fundamental keyboard skills for music majors and minors with prior keyboard experience. Students will learn major scales and arpeggios, simple chord progressions, 12-Bar blues, sight-reading skills, fundamentals of harmonization and transposition at the keyboard, and the basics of music improvisation.

Prerequisites: MUS 116

MUS 118 PIANO TECHNIQUES1 Credit

Development of keyboard skills for music majors. Students will learn harmonic minor scales and arpeggios, sight-reading, harmonizations and transpositions that include 7th chords, complex chord progressions, basics of instrumental and choral score reading, improvisation, and basic accompanying skills.

Prerequisites: MUS 117 or permission of the instructor

MUS 120 CHADRON STATE COMMUNITY CHORUS0-1 Credits

The Chadron Community Chorus is a choir of mixed voices and is open to all students and community members without audition. This choir performs a wide array of literature from standard to contemporary choral repertoire and gives at least one concert performance each semester.

Notes: This course may be taken for repeated credit.

Requirements: All students who are enrolled full-time must take this course for credit.

MUS 121 CHADRON STATE COMMUNITY SYMPHONIC BAND0-1 Credits

Open to all students and community members. This ensemble gives a minimum of one concert performance each semester.

Notes: This course may be taken for repeated credit.

Requirements: All students who are enrolled full-time must take this course for credit.

MUS 122 CSC REGIONAL JAZZ BAND0-1 Credits

The CSC Regional Jazz Band brings together college students, area high school students, and community members to study, rehearse, and perform jazz music. Open to all who qualify by audition. This ensemble gives a minimum of one concert performance each semester.

Notes: This course may be taken for repeated credit.

Requirements: All students who are enrolled full-time must take this course for credit.

MUS 126 EAGLE BAND0-1 Credits

Open to all students who qualify by audition. The Eagle Band serves the college and community through performance at parades, football games, and basketball games.

MUS 131 THEORY I3 Credits

This course focuses on the rudiments of Western classical music, including intervals, chords, and scales, and introduces students to the principles of tonal harmony.

Prerequisites: MUS 112 or permission of music theory coordinator

Co-requisites: MUS 131L and MUS 117.

MUS 131L AURAL SKILLS I1 Credit

Development of aural skills through singing and active listening. Topics are coordinated with the content of Theory I.

Co-requisites: MUS 131

MUS 132 THEORY II3 Credits

Basic principles of Western harmony, utilizing and analytical and compositional skills to develop an understanding of structural components in tonal music.

Prerequisites: MUS 131 and MUS 131L

Co-requisites: MUS 132L and MUS 118

MUS 132L AURAL SKILLS II1 Credit

This course focuses on the development of aural skills through singing and active listening. Topics are coordinated with the content of Theory II.

Prerequisites: MUS 131L

Co-requisites: MUS 132

MUS 149 EAGLE DRUM LINE1 Credit

The CSC Eagle Drum Line performs at events sponsored by various organizations on the CSC campus and also at events sponsored by groups and institutions off-campus. Events may include but are not limited to CSC sporting events, parades, pep rallies, grand openings, conferences, faculty meetings, and other events by request.

Add Consent: Instructor Consent

Requirements: Open to students who qualify by audition. Previous experience in music is required.

MUS 155 MUSIC TECHNOLOGY2 Credits

Technology is now an integral part of any career in music. Knowledge of sound files, notation software, and sound reinforcement is essential for any professionals in the field. This class will explore programs that are vital within the music industry.

MUS 156 MUSIC TECHNOLOGY IN EDUCATION3 Credits

Current and future music educators are in perpetual need of developing new techniques in the music classroom. Innovations can continue to be developed through the use of computer programs designed to enhance pedagogy in the music curriculum, PK-12. This class will not only explore programs that meet the current industry standard, but also include study of freeware available for programs on a budget.

MUS 215ZZ PRIVATE MUSIC EVENT SUPPORT1 Credit

In this course, students will apply their knowledge of music technology in support of music events. Sound reinforcement and online streaming will be a focus of students' efforts. Students will be involved in additional aspects of support for music events, including the setup of instruments and the promotion of the events.

Prerequisites: MUS 155 or MUS 156

MUS 216 GUITAR CLASS3 Credits

Beginner-level guitar instruction designed for the non-music major student. The basic elements of playing the guitar, including both chordal and solo techniques. Guitars are provided.

MUS 220 FUNCTIONAL PIANO2 Credits

Students will develop skills in nine areas of keyboard playing: (1) harmonization,

(2) improvisation, (3) sight-reading, (4) instrumental and (5) choral score-reading, (6) performance of major and minor scales, (7) transposition, (8) playing by ear, and (9) repertoire preparation.

Prerequisites: MUS 118 or departmental approval

Co-requisites: MUS 298

MUS 227 SURVEY OF MUSIC HISTORY3 Credits

Survey of Music History will examine the history of Western Classical music, including the Medieval, Renaissance, Baroque, Classical, and Romantic periods, considering cultural, social, economic, psychological, and political factors.

Prerequisites: MUS 131

MUS 231 THEORY III3 Credits

This course applies the skills learned in Theory I and II to the structural level, exploring approaches to chromaticism and modulation, and utilizing these techniques through composition and analysis of Baroque, Classical, and Romantic forms.

Prerequisites: MUS 132 and MUS 132L

Co-requisites: MUS 231L and MUS 220

MUS 231L AURAL SKILLS III1 Credit

This course focuses on the development of aural skills through singing and active listening. Content includes chromaticism, secondary functions, modulations, mixed meter, and open-spaced sonorities.

Prerequisites: MUS 132L

MUS 232 POST-TONAL THEORY2 Credits

This course introduces and explores a broad range of analytical and compositional techniques and issues relevant to twentieth-century music. Topics will include pitch-class set theory, atonality, 12-tone techniques, serialism, and polytonality, and will include synthesizing concepts in compositions.

Prerequisites: MUS 131 and Sophomore or above status

MUS 233 MUSIC FOR THE CLASSROOM TEACHER3 Credits

Materials and methods pertaining to the integration of music in the elementary classroom. Stresses demonstration and class participation.

Notes: It is strongly recommended that students with no background in music take MUS 112 prior to taking MUS 233.

Requirements: Required for all elementary education majors.

MUS 234 WORLD MUSIC3 Credits

This course will take you on a musical journey to many regions of the world including Sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East, the Caribbean, South America, and Asia. In this course, you will develop the ability to hear and discuss the elements of music, gain an appreciation for differing cultural values, and learn the significance of music as a cultural and aesthetic expression.

MUS 235 MUSIC APPRECIATION3 Credits

This course focuses on how to listen to and appreciate the human and cultural values of various styles of music as well as learning the significance of music as cultural and aesthetic expression.

Notes: For non-music majors.

MUS 236 TOPICS IN MUSIC0-3 Credits

To meet the specific needs of a group of students by studying areas of music not presented in the curriculum. The class will include lecture, demonstrations, writing, and performance.

Notes: May be repeated with different emphasis.

MUS 240 PRINCIPLES OF CONDUCTING2 Credits

A study of basic conducting techniques. Emphasis is placed upon the mastery of simple patterns, cues and expressive gestures and on common problems in leading group singing and in directing musical ensembles.

MUS 241 SURVEY OF LYRIC DICTION2 Credits

This course offers a survey of lyric diction of Latin and Italian. The International Phonetic Alphabet will be used in analyzing song texts in terms of diction and pronunciation.

Prerequisites: Sophomore or above status

MUS 250 MUSIC EDUCATION PRACTICUM, VOCAL1 Credit

Techniques of voice production. Will include evaluations of the scientific, psychological, physiological, and empirical methods of teaching voice. Techniques of developing the young voice will be emphasized. This course is offered in the fall of odd-numbered years.

Notes: This course is offered in the fall of odd-numbered years.

MUS 251 MUSIC EDUCATION PRACTICUM, FIELD0-1 Credits

Introduction to the study of the voice, wind, percussion, and string instruments. Students will gain practical performing skills for public school teachers.

Notes: May be taken for repeated credit.

MUS 252 MUSIC EDUCATION PRACTICUM, VOCAL1 Credit

Students will complete any remaining student learning outcomes introduced in MUS 250.

Prerequisites: MUS 250

MUS 267 THE VIRTUAL MUSICIAN3 Credits

In this course, we will explore how to create, sample, mix, loop, and edit digital music using GarageBand. This course is designed for non music majors. No prior music reading or playing skills are necessary.

MUS 268 BASIC PIANO SKILLS3 Credits

Beginning-level group piano instruction for students with no prior piano playing experience. This course is designed for non music majors. No prior music reading or playing skills are necessary.

MUS 299 SOPHOMORE QUALIFYING EXAM0 Credits

Performance assessment required of all music majors prior to enrollment into upper-division private music instruction. A student must have a cumulative GPA of 3.00 on his/her major instrument or voice (MUS 115/215) to present the qualifying exam.

Prerequisites: MUS 199 and at least one prior semester of MUS 215

Co-requisites: MUS 220 and 2 credit hours of MUS 215 concurrently

Individual instruction in composition and/or analysis. Students will set semester goals in conjunction with the instructor.

Individual instruction in piano, voice, percussion, brass instruments, woodwind instruments, guitar and bass.

MUS 315R SURVEY OF INSTRUMENT REPAIR TECHNIQUES1-2 Credits

This laboratory course is designed to introduce students to repair techniques for the most common wind band instruments. Students will learn about the mechanical properties, the assessment of playing condition, and basic techniques for repairing instruments.

Prerequisites: Sophomore or above status

MUS 315S PRIVATE MUSIC INSTRUCTION/VOICE1-2 Credits

Individual instruction in piano, voice, percussion, brass instruments, woodwind instruments, guitar and bass.

Prerequisites: MUS 299 and Sophomore or above status

Individual instruction in piano, voice, percussion, brass instruments, woodwind instruments, guitar and bass.

Add Consent: Department Consent

MUS 315V PRIVATE RECORDING TECHNIQUES1-2 Credits

An introduction to recording techniques using computer-based digital recording with standard software. This course will prepare students to produce demo records and include training in studio setup, signal flow, microphone placement, editing, plug-ins and mixing.

Prerequisites: Music major and Sophomore or above status

Notes: Open to all music majors or by permission of the instructor.

MUS 315X PRIVATE JAZZ IMPROVISATION1-2 Credits

Individual instruction in piano, organ, voice, percussion, brass instruments, woodwind instruments, and stringed instruments.

Prerequisites: MUS 299 and Sophomore or above status

Co-requisites: MUS 101

Add Consent: Department Consent

MUS 315ZZ PRIVATE MUSIC EVENT MANAGEMENT1 Credit

In this course, the student will apply their knowledge of music technology, sound reinforcement, and the music industry in the planning and management of a music event. The student will organize performers, coordinate with a venue, and solicit music industry student support to run the event. The student will also be in charge of communicating information about the event for promotion of it.

Prerequisites: MUS 215ZZ

Co-requisites: MUS 342 and MUS 345

MUS 321 CHORAL CONDUCTING2 Credits

Study of conducting techniques and choral literature.

Prerequisites: MUS 240 and Sophomore or above status

Co-requisites: MUS 220 and MUS 251, MUS 252, MUS 351, or MUS 352

MUS 322 INSTRUMENTAL CONDUCTING2 Credits

Techniques of conducting instrumental organizations and the study of instrumental literature.

Prerequisites: MUS 240 and Sophomore or above status

Co-requisites: MUS 220 and MUS 251, MUS 252, MUS 351, or MUS 352

MUS 326 EAGLE BAND1 Credit

Open to all students who qualify by audition. The Eagle Band serves the college and community through performance at parades, football games, and basketball games.

Prerequisites: Sophomore or above status

MUS 330 AMERICAN POPULAR MUSIC3 Credits

A perspective of the history of American popular music that combines the study of cultural and social history with an analytical study of music styles. This course identifies three streams (African, European, and Latin American) of musical characteristics found in American popular music and traces the evolution of these characteristics from their origins beginning in the mid-18th century into the 21st century. Critical listening skills are learned through the practice of listening and sharing what is heard through discussions using a common music vocabulary.

Prerequisites: Sophomore or above status

MUS 335 RECORDING TECHNIQUES I2 Credits

An introduction to recording techniques using computer-based digital recording with other software. This course will prepare students to operate Pro Tools recording software and will include training in editing, MIDI, using plug-ins and mixing.

Notes: Open to all music majors and non-majors.

MUS 340 BUSINESS OF PRIVATE TEACHING3 Credits

Practical issues of operating an independent music teaching studio. Issues such as recruitment, retention, contracts, studio policies, income tax and maintaining consistent monthly income will be discussed in depth.

Prerequisites: Sophomore or above status

MUS 341 MUSIC INDUSTRY I3 Credits

How the music industry operates, with emphasis on the record industry, publishing/songwriting, copyright, merchandising, retail, and marketing. Musical aspects, as well as business and legal aspects are examined.

MUS 342 MUSIC INDUSTRY II3 Credits

A study of the music industry including career options, music products, booking and promoting concerts, independent artist strategies, and developing a music business plan.

Prerequisites: MUS 341

MUS 345 RECORDING TECHNIQUES II2 Credits

This course will teach students to produce their own recordings and include training in studio setup, signal flow, microphone placement and other studio audio recording techniques.

Prerequisites: MUS 335 and sophomore or above status

MUS 349 EAGLE DRUM LINE1 Credit

The CSC Eagle Drum Line performs at events sponsored by various organizations on the CSC campus and also at events sponsored by groups and institutions off-campus. Events may include but are not limited to CSC sporting events, parades, pep rallies, grand openings, conferences, faculty meetings, and other events by request.

Prerequisites: Sophomore or above status

Requirements: Open to students who qualify by audition. Previous experience in music is required.

MUS 351 MUSIC EDUCATION PRACTICUM FIELD1 Credit

Continuation of MUS 251. Students will gain more practical performing experience, but will also begin peer teaching in these areas.

Prerequisites: Sophomore or above status

Notes: May be taken for repeated credit.

MUS 352 MUSIC EDUCATION PRACTICUM, FIELD1 Credit

Culmination of the MUS 251 and 351 courses. Students will complete the remaining student learning outcomes introduced in MUS 251 and 351.

Prerequisites: MUS 351 and Sophomore or above status

MUS 357 INSTRUMENTATION & ARRANGING2 Credits

This course provides an overview of the characteristics for instruments of the wind band and orchestra, and introduces the student to techniques of scoring for a variety of instrumental combinations. Students will also explore challenges typically encountered in elementary and secondary instrumental ensembles.

Prerequisites: MUS 131 and Sophomore or above status

MUS 362 KEYBOARD SKILLS FOR THE CLASSROOM TEACHER2 Credits

Refinement of keyboard skills with direct application to the music education environment, with emphasis in harmonization, score reading and accompanying.

Prerequisites: A grade of "B" or better in MUS 220 or permission of the instructor and sophomore or above status

MUS 379 POST-TONAL HISTORY AND THEORY3 Credits

This course examines the broad range of compositional techniques and historical developments relevant to the music of the twentieth century. The course will explore atonality, polytonality, neoclassicism, serialism, experimental music, minimalism, electronic music, and spectral music. Theoretical topics will include pitch-class set theory, 12-tone techniques, modes and scales, and quartal and quintal harmonies.

Prerequisites: MUS 131

MUS 390 INTERNSHIP IN MUSIC1-12 Credits

Provides practical experience in the music products industry or the entertainment industry.

Prerequisites: Sophomore or above status

Add Consent: Department Consent

Notes: Interested students should contact the Internship and Career Services Office to secure application materials; application should be made prior to the semester the internship will be started; the amount of credit will be based on the availability of a suitable work position, the qualifications of the applicant and the work hours.

MUS 399 SOLO HALF-RECITAL0 Credits

A 25 to 30 minute solo performance. The performing student must have a cumulative GPA of 3.00 on his/her major instrument or voice (MUS 115/215/315) in order to present the recital. Additionally, the student must receive the recommendation of the private instructor and the collective music faculty at a pre-recital hearing held at least three weeks prior to the scheduled recital date.

Prerequisites: At least one prior semester of MUS 315 and sophomore or above status

Co-requisites: 2 credit hours of MUS 315 concurrently

MUS 400 INDEPENDENT STUDY OR RESEARCH1-3 Credits

Study or research in an area of special interest.

Prerequisites: Junior or above status

Add Consent: Instructor Consent

Notes: The number of credit hours is determined by the topic and the amount of work required.

Requirements: Permission of Instructor, Dean and Academic Vice President is required.

MUS 402 WIND SYMPHONY0 Credits

Open to all students who qualify by audition. This ensemble gives a minimum of one concert performance each semester.

Notes: This 400-level course is a 0 credit option available only to music education majors who have successfully completed MUS 299-Sophomore Qualifying Exam.

MUS 413 JAZZ AND POP ARRANGING2 Credits

The course covers harmonies with upper extensions, rhythm section writing, and instrument ranges for all sections of the jazz big band. Additionally, students will study approaches to harmonization and arranging in jazz, culminating in a big band arrangement.

Prerequisites: MUS 131 and Junior or above status

MUS 430 TOPICS IN MUSIC0-3 Credits

Examines a special topic in music. Topics vary from semester to semester. May be repeated.

Prerequisites: Junior or above status

MUS 431A ELEMENTARY MUSIC METHODS2 Credits

An instructional methods course in the major field of content specialization required of music education majors pursuing content area endorsement in PK-12 Vocal Music and a field endorsement in PK-12 Music.

Prerequisites: Junior or above status

MUS 431C SECONDARY CHORALE METHODS2 Credits

An instructional methods course in vocal music required of music education majors pursuing a vocal music endorsement for PK-12 or a music field endorsement for PK-12.

Prerequisites: Junior or above status

MUS 431D SECONDARY INSTRUMENTAL METHODS2 Credits

An instructional methods course in instrumental music required of music education majors pursuing music field endorsement for PK-12.

Prerequisites: Junior or above status

MUS 432 TOPICS IN MUSIC HISTORY AND LITERATURE2 Credits

The course focuses on various topics through the lens of music history. Topics will consider the social, cultural, economic, and political factors of the course's focus.

Prerequisites: MUS 131 and Junior or above status

Notes: Since the topics rotate and will not duplicate more than once every four semesters, this course may be taken for repeated credit.

Prerequisites: Junior or above status
